summary: Taj Mahal is a classic Knizia design where players bid across multiple simultaneous auctions each round using a hand of cards, competing to control regions and collect commodities that convert to influence points. It's tense and cutthroat, with every auction affecting your standing relative to your neighbors.
praised: High player interaction and tough decisions
Elegant design that rewards reading opponents
criticised: Can feel mean or kingmaking in some groups
Auction mechanism takes a play or two to click

interaction.detail: Players bid against each other for regional control and palace-building rights using cards from a shared hand, directly blocking or outbidding rivals each round. The shared board state of regional influence markers means every win or loss directly affects everyone else's position.

scoring.why: Points come from winning provinces via card auctions, building palaces from consecutive province wins, and holding majorities in collected commodities, three fairly distinct engines.
scoring.how_you_win: Bid influence cards to win control of each region (or peel off to collect commodities instead), build palaces when you win regions in a row, and end up with the most combined influence and commodity points.
